Can't tell from here. The concrete cost of being wrong: users can't log in, locked out of the system.

Settling it: query your user table for any usernames matching `[^a-z0-9_]` (contains dots, capitals, or other characters). Something like:

```sql
SELECT username FROM users WHERE username NOT REGEXP '^[a-z0-9_]{3,20}$';
```

Or in your ORM, filter for usernames that fail the regex. If that query returns rows, the new validation will break existing accounts.
